findings.title: No load-test tier for new concurrency/stream paths
findings.description: The testing rules require a `tests/load/` tier for code on concurrency/network paths, and this slice is squarely there: `dispatch()` now multiplexes a live SDK stream, per-message idle timeouts (`asyncio.timeout` around each `anext`), background-agent bookkeeping, and `stop_task` control requests (src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:222-344). Unit tests with `ScriptedClient` verify functional behavior but cannot catch event-loop starvation, timer/cancellation contention, or budget overruns under a realistic stream. No `tests/load/` directory exists in the repo. The rules say CI must gate load tests for slices touching these paths.

findings.title: `background_tasks_waited` docstring overstates what it counts
findings.description: The session attribute comment says "background agents it waited for", but the value assigned in `dispatch()`'s `finally` is `turns.ledger.seen_count` — "distinct waited-for agents *ever tracked*", including ones that started and finished entirely within the foreground turn (never waited on). `BackgroundLedger.seen_count` documents this correctly; the session field comment drifts. Minor, but the metadata key `background_tasks_waited` written into `ActionResult.metadata` inherits the same imprecision.

findings.title: Cancelled stream iterator abandoned on idle timeout
findings.description: When `asyncio.timeout(idle_s)` expires, the pending `anext(stream)` is cancelled and the async generator from `receive_response()` is abandoned mid-iteration; `_collect_turns` then returns via `_stop_background` without closing it, and the next `dispatch()` opens a fresh iterator. I could not verify from the SDK source available here whether a cancelled-and-abandoned `receive_response()` iterator leaks a queued message or emits warnings on collection — flagging as unverified rather than asserting a defect. A defensive `finally: await stream.aclose()` (or a comment that the SDK iterator tolerates abandonment) would close the question.

findings.title: Silently dropped resume seed when no session ever connects
findings.description: If `start_from` produced a `resume_seed` but the run is resumed under a path where no SDK session is ever connected (e.g. all steps route to non-SDK, or `_step_needs_sdk` cannot statically confirm a pool candidate), the seed is discarded with no log line. This is defensible — there is no session to seed — but it differs from the "never use silent fallback" convention; a DEBUG log ("resume seed dropped: no SDK session connected") would make the discard observable.

findings.title: `open_pipeline_session` suppresses a pyright argument-type error
findings.description: `setting_sources=settings["setting_sources"],  # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]` works around an SDK stub mismatch rather than fixing it at the boundary. Given the project targets zero pyright errors as a merge blocker, an inline ignore is debt; a local narrow (e.g. `cast` with a comment naming the SDK stub limitation) would keep strict mode honest.

findings.title: `sdk_session.py` has grown past the ~300-line file guideline
findings.description: The file is now ~490 lines versus the project's ~300-line guideline, and `executor.py` (~950 lines) was already well past it. The extraction of `sdk_turns.py` and `text_tail.py` was the right move and offsets the growth; a further split of the turn-reading loop (`_collect_turns`/`_read_turn*`) into its own module would bring it back under the guideline.

findings.title: Settings policy is single-sourced and mechanically enforced
findings.description: `pipeline_setting_sources` / `REVIEW_SETTING_SOURCES` / `sdk_settings_options` centralize what was previously a scattered `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY` literal plus per-caller env merging. Every consumer (pipeline session, one-shot dispatch, reviews, provider) now routes through it, the test matrix in `tests/providers/sdk/test_settings_policy.py` drives each real builder, and the old duplicated env-merge logic in `provider.py` was removed rather than left alongside. No drift found.

findings.title: Exception handling and observability conform to the project rules
findings.description: Every broad catch carries a specific justification comment and the correct treatment: `_reconnect` logs at ERROR via `logger.exception` and re-raises (also recording `unusable_reason` so later calls fail loudly rather than silently); `_stop_background`'s `except Exception` documents why no narrower type exists and logs each failure; the executor's lazy-connect failure logs at ERROR and re-raises as `LazySessionConnectError`. New failure modes (stream end with agents running, leftover follow-up turn, idle timeout) all emit WARNING-level signals and each has a test asserting the observable output — matching the failure-mode-enumeration rule.

findings.title: Bool config coercion and typed reads are correct including the bool/int subclass trap
findings.description: `_coerce_bool` handles case/whitespace leniently and names the key in the error; `get_typed_config` checks `type_ is bool` before the int check with an explicit comment on `bool` being an `int` subclass, and rejects `1`/`0` written directly into TOML for a bool key (covered by `test_typed_read_rejects_non_bool`). The CLI's `_display_value` renders TOML spelling consistently for both `get` and `list`.

structured_findings.summary: No load-test tier for new concurrency/stream paths
Cancelled stream iterator abandoned on idle timeout
Silently dropped resume seed when no session ever connects
`sdk_session.py` has grown past the ~300-line file guideline
Settings policy is single-sourced and mechanically enforced
Exception handling and observability conform to the project rules
Bool config coercion and typed reads are correct including the bool/int subclass trap
